intro: For a linear classifier, sensitivity is determined by the weights of the selected class. Pair that gradient with the observed input.
task: Return selected class scores, input gradients, and input-times-gradient attributions.
requirements: features has shape batch-by-features and weights features-by-classes. classes has one integer class index per example. No bias is used.
Return {"scores": vector, "gradient": batch-by-features matrix, "input_times_gradient": matrix}. Different examples may request different classes.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Different classes
examples.output:
{'scores': [5.0, 9.0],
 'gradient': [[1.0, 2.0], [-1.0, 3.0]],
 'input_times_gradient': [[1.0, 4.0], [-3.0, 12.0]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: The derivative of a weighted sum with respect to one input is its coefficient.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: Gather weight columns per example, then transpose the gathered result.

explanation: Input gradients measure local score sensitivity. For an affine function the gradient does not depend on the input location, although the requested class determines which weight column is relevant.
Multiplying the gradient by the input gives a zero-baseline contribution. Its row sum recovers the bias-free score; absolute gradients would lose that signed reconstruction.
